title: Generating stable isolated mitochondrial recipient clones in mammalian cells using MitoPunch mitochondrial transfer
protocol: Harvest mitochondrial donor cells.
Aspirate culture medium from T-225 flasks.
Pipette 20 mL DPBS into each flask.
Release cells from the flasks using a cell scraper.
Suspend scraped cells in DPBS and collect into 50 mL conical tubes.
Centrifuge tubes at 500 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant.
Wash cell pellets in 10 mL DPBS and centrifuge again at 500 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant.
Disrupt mitochondrial donor cells using the Qiagen Qproteome Mitochondrial Isolation Kit.
Resuspend cell pellets in ice-cold Lysis Buffer at a concentration of ∼1 × 10^7 cells per mL and transfer to 2 mL tubes.
Prepare Lysis Buffer with 1:100 Protease Inhibitor Solution prior to resuspension.
Incubate on end-over-end shaker for 10 min at 4°C.
Centrifuge the samples at 1000 × g for 10 min at 4°C and aspirate supernatant without disrupting the pellet.
Resuspend each cell pellet in 1.5 mL ice cold Disruption Buffer with a 1 mL pipette tip.
Prepare Disruption Buffer with 1:100 Protease Inhibitor Solution prior to resuspension.
Disrupt cells using a blunt-ended 26G needle attached to a 3 mL Luer-Lok syringe.
Slowly pull the entire lysate into the syringe and expel the volume 10 times, avoiding the formation of bubbles in the suspension.
Centrifuge lysate at 1000 × g for 10 min at 4°C and transfer supernatant to a new sterile 1.5 mL tube.
Optional: Repeat this step to reduce the probability of intact cells contaminating the mitochondrial preparation.
Centrifuge the supernatant at 6000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Carefully aspirate supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 1 mL Mitochondrial Storage Buffer using a 1 mL pipette tip and centrifuge at 6000 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Prepare the MitoPunch apparatus during this centrifugation step to minimize time between resuspension of mitochondrial isolate and MitoPunch transfer.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend the mitochondrial pellet in a volume of DPBS with calcium and magnesium equal to 120 μL times the number of MitoPunch replicates.
Mix isolated mitochondria with a PDMS reservoir.
Seal the PDMS reservoir to a cell culture filter insert seeded with recipient cells.
Activate the solenoid to drive the mechanical plunger into the PDMS reservoir.
Increase internal pressure in the PDMS reservoir, forcing mitochondrial suspension through the filter insert pores.
Deliver mitochondrial suspension directly into the recipient cell cytoplasm.
Keep the isolated mitochondrial sample on ice during MitoPunch transfers.
Minimize the time that isolated mitochondria are kept on ice before transfer.
Spray 70% ethanol into a tissue.
Wipe down the MitoPunch apparatus with the treated tissue.
Place the MitoPunch apparatus inside a biosafety cabinet.
Connect the MitoPunch apparatus to a breadboard.
Connect the breadboard to a power supply.
Plug the power supply into a 120 V wall outlet.
Test piston actuation to ensure device has power.
Remove a sterile PDMS reservoir from an autoclave bag.
Place the PDMS reservoir on the MitoPunch apparatus.
Wash the PDMS reservoir three times with 120 μL DPBS containing calcium and magnesium.
Pipette up and down three times during each wash to cover the entire surface area of the reservoir.
Pipette 120 μL of mitochondrial suspension or DPBS control into the PDMS reservoir.
Remove a 12-well dish with recipient-cell-seeded filter inserts from the incubator.
Place the 12-well dish inside the biosafety cabinet.
Use sterile forceps to remove one filter insert from the dish.
Secure the filter insert into the top plate of the MitoPunch apparatus by placing its plastic wings on the remaining ring.
Carefully screw the top internal ring until it is tight against the filter wings.
Lower the top plate along the optomechanical assembly rods such that the filter insert contacts the PDMS reservoir.
Ensure the filter insert is firmly pressed against the PDMS to create a seal.
Actuate the MitoPunch piston using the switch on the breadboard.
Maintain gentle pressure on the top plate with your hand while actuating the solenoid to keep the seal between the filter insert and the PDMS intact.
Leave the piston in the protracted position for 3 seconds, then release the piston switch.
Remove the filter insert from the apparatus carefully.
Replace the filter insert in its original medium within the 12-well dish.
Place the 12-well dish in a humidified 37°C incubator for 2 hours prior to collecting recipient cells.
Aspirate the medium from the wells containing the filter inserts.
Carefully aspirate the medium from inside the filter insert without touching the cell layer on the PET membrane.
Aspirate the medium from outside the filter insert, ensuring you collect any medium retained at the contact point between the bottom of the filter insert and the well.
Change aspirator tip between samples.
Wash filter inserts with DPBS without calcium and magnesium.
Apply 0.5 mL DPBS gently to the filter insert.
Apply 1.5 mL DPBS to the well outside the filter insert.
Aspirate DPBS from within the filter insert carefully.
Aspirate any residual liquid retained between the bottom of the filter and the well.
Change aspirator tip between samples.
Apply Accutase dissociation reagent to the filters.
Incubate for 5 min in a 37°C humidified incubator.
Pipette 0.5 mL Accutase to the filter insert.
Pipette 1.5 mL Accutase to the well outside the filter insert.
Visually inspect the plate under an inverted microscope.
Return plate to the incubator for 3 min if dissociation is incomplete.
Repeat until cells have released from the membrane.
Release cells from the membrane.
Apply 0.5 mL of uridine-supplemented medium to the filter insert.
Gently disrupt the cell layer using a 1 mL pipette tip.
Pipette the full volume from the filter insert into a 10 cm dish containing 10 mL warm uridine-supplemented complete medium.
Place the 10 cm dishes in a 37°C humidified incubator.
Culture recipient cells in dialyzed, nucleotide-free selection medium for clone isolation.
Incubate the 10 cm dishes of MitoPunch recipient cells in a 37°C humidified incubator with uridine-supplemented complete medium for 3 days following transfer.
Monitor confluence daily and do not allow cultures to exceed 80% confluence.
Exchange the complete medium for SIMR selection medium if cultures reach >80% confluence.
Exchange the medium daily with 10 mL fresh SIMR selection medium.
Record the confluence of the ρ0 negative control plate daily.
Continue feeding cells with SIMR selection medium until the ρ0 control plate is no longer viable.
Proceed to clone isolation or crystal violet staining as soon as the control plate is no longer viable.
At 5 days post-delivery, feed cells with galactose SIMR selection medium if required by recipient cell sensitivity conditions.
Exchange the selection medium daily during galactose selection until the DPBS control transfer has completely died.
After death of the control, exchange the selection medium for SIMR selection medium to allow clones to grow large enough to harvest.
Isolate SIMR clones from 10 cm dishes after the selection process.
Passage isolated SIMR clones onto 6-well dishes for expansion before they overgrow.
Select clones that are not adjacent to or in contact with other clones for isolation.
Aspirate the medium from the dish and wash with 5 ml of DPBS.
Aspirate the DPBS from the dish.
Coat one side of a cylinder in sterilized high-vacuum grease.
Gently adhere each cylinder to the dish, fully encompassing one clone within the cylinder.
Slowly add 200 μl of Accutase to each cylinder and incubate for 5 min in a 37°C humidified incubator.
Verify that the cells have fully dissociated from the dish under an inverted microscope.
Incubate cells for another 3 min if they have not fully dissociated.
Move the cell suspension into a well of a 6-well dish containing 2 mL of warm complete medium using a micropipettor.
Incubate newly plated clones in a 37°C humidified incubator.
Aspirate the medium from the plate carefully to avoid disturbing the clones.
Apply 1 mL of freshly diluted 4% paraformaldehyde to the dish and tilt to fully coat the surface.
Incubate at room temperature (RT) in a chemical fume hood for 15 min.
Aspirate the 4% paraformaldehyde from the dish and dispose of it in the appropriate chemical waste container.
Apply 2 mL of crystal violet solution to each plate and tilt to fully coat.
Incubate at RT in the chemical fume hood for 30 min.
Remove excess crystal violet using a serological pipette and dispose of it in the appropriate chemical waste container.
Rinse each plate twice with DI water to remove excess crystal violet solution.
Dry plates upside-down on an absorbent surface to allow any residual crystal violet solution to drip off the plate.
Store plates away from light until ready to analyze.
